column1: # UnitTypeSlots batch: owner <TAB> kind <TAB> old <TAB> descriptor <TAB> semantic name
# Slot order is fixed by the constructor, so the two rulesets that build it name every slot:
#   DsfRuleset: general, humvee, battleTank, artillery, missileTank, fourByFour, baseStation,
#               shipyard, airfield, oilField, transport, carrier, chinnook, fighterPlane,
#               helicopter, cruiser, submarine, gunboat, mechanic, hovercraft, truck
#   TsfRuleset: general, battleTank, battleTank, artillery, missileTank, null, baseStation,
#               shipyard, airfield, null, transport, carrier, airship, fighterPlane,
#               helicopter, cruiser, submarine, destroyer, null, null, null
# Slots the two rulesets fill differently keep the Desert Stormfront name (slot 2 humvee vs
# battleTank, slot 18 gunboat vs destroyer); the class JavaDoc records the Tsf counterpart.
# Cross-check: IntentEvaluator compares getUnitTypeSlots().t() against IntentType.Truck, so the
# last getter (which returns field u) is the truck. Field t (hovercraft) has no getter.
# Nothing reads these slots by name - ModRuleset builds them from a positional JSON array, so
# renaming cannot change saved data or mod behaviour.
